description.narrative: Following on from the programme design workshop and initial assessments by Arup Oxfam in Uganda will be conducting research on governance approaches and willingness to pay. Update on development A draft results framework was developed in conjunction with Arup, the Regional WASH Adviser and the Uganda country office WASH team and Conflict Adviser. Following the development of the draft resultsframework Arup undertook initial assessments covering; Socio – economic, governance profile and a risk assessment. This used previous studies, the rapid assessment conducted by Oxfam, Government documents and programmatic outlines to provide insight into these areas. Next steps The work was completed in January and in a follow up discussion a decision was made to build on this evidence with agovernance review to investigate further the following gaps: • Mapping of the main water resources and its situation • More detail on the challenges to ensure long-term sustainability of the water supply and services. •Confirm which stakeholders are active in Karamoja (or most actives) and the relationship/linkages between them. • Information on the different water models used in Karamoja (challenges and strengths). • Community perception on the benefits of reliable water supply and the performance of the current water services. • Information on the progress of existing water and resilience projects and main challenges faced. As well as other projects planned in the region. • Information on current situation of theUmbrella Karamoja. WSUP has professionalised the Mid-Western Umbrella and the MWE was planning to replicate the programme in 2022 in the other Umbrellas (World Bank funding). • Ability and willingness to pay analysis in the rural and urban communities inKaramoja. Information on current emergency livestock programming for droughts, and use of international humanitarian standards (Livestock Emergency Guidelines and Standards) or other standards

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
